properties.title: Special Marine Warning issued November 1 at 1:46AM CDT until November 1 at 1:45AM CST by NWS Mobile AL
properties.description:
SMWMOB

The National Weather Service in Mobile has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Pensacola FL from 20 to
60 NM...

* Until 145 AM CST.

* At 145 AM CDT, a strong thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located 29 nm south of Okaloosa Deep Water Reef, or
54 nm south of Destin, moving west at 10 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* The strong thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.
properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.
properties.area: Waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Pensacola FL from 20 to 60 NM

properties.title: Special Marine Warning issued November 1 at 1:17AM CDT until November 1 at 1:45AM CST by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
SMWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Waters from Mexico Beach to Apalachicola FL from 20 to 60 NM...

* Until 145 AM CST.

* At 116 AM CDT, a strong thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located 17 nm southwest of Empire Mica Wreck. The
severe thunderstorm was nearly stationary.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats...damage
vessels...and create suddenly higher waves. Make sure all
on board are in a secure location and wearing life
jackets. Expect wind gusts in excess of 34
knots...suddenly higher waves...frequent lightning...and
heavy downpours. Make sure all on board are wearing life
jackets.

* The severe thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.
properties.instruction: Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

forecast.

forecast.

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued October 30 at 11:47AM MDT until November 3 at 5:00AM MST by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a Flood
Advisory for the following rivers in New Mexico...

Animas River At Farmington affecting San Juan County.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Animas River at Farmington.

* WHEN...From this morning to late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...At 10.0 feet, Portions of the riverwalk in Farmington are
flooded. Local overbank flooding is occurring along the lower
Animas River.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:30 AM MDT Friday the stage was 6.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 9.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 9.0 feet Monday
afternoon. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Action stage is 9.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 10.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

If you are in the advisory area, remain alert to possible flooding or
the possibility of the advisory being upgraded to a warning.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

The next statement will be issued Saturday afternoon at noon MDT.
